issues.failure_explanation: TensorRIP does not bound the ambient operator norm, so the stated fitting tolerance is insufficient. Let D=Σ_i e_i^{⊗d}, v=Vec(D)/√n, and AᵀA=I+cnvvᵀ. Its rank-3 RIP constant is at most 3c, while its operator norm grows with n. For X*=e_1^{⊗d}, a fitting rule that returns −X* and then remains there satisfies the displayed approximation condition for sufficiently large n: the pre-threshold error has norm of order c√n. Nevertheless, the noiseless residual does not contract.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the fitting tolerance by the operator-norm-dependent σ(a) already displayed in the theorem, and use that strengthened hypothesis consistently.
issues.overall_effect: The stated TIHT convergence theorem allows approximation operators for which its recovery conclusion is false.
issues.title: TIHT fitting accuracy omits the necessary operator-norm dependence
issues.why_classification: The repair materially strengthens the fitting requirement, potentially by a dimension-dependent factor, but preserves the convergence rate and existing proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let  $\mat{A} \in \R^{m \times n_1 n_2 \dots n_d}$ be a measurement matrix whose rows consist of randomly sampled independent sub-Gaussian vectors.
Examples of sub-Gaussian random variables include Gaussian, Bernoulli and all bounded random variables.

issues.failure_explanation: Independent sub-Gaussian rows need not have identity second moment. Zero rows satisfy the stated hypotheses but never give RIP for δ<1, regardless of m. Likewise, rescaling an isotropic distribution changes the limiting squared embedding norm. The same deficient measurement model is used in both RIP statements.

failure_location.quote: Let  $\mat{A} \in \R^{m \times n_1 n_2 \dots n_d}$ be a measurement matrix whose rows consist of randomly sampled independent sub-Gaussian vectors.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require independent isotropic sub-Gaussian rows, for example mean-zero rows with covariance I, in the common measurement model and both theorem statements.
issues.overall_effect: Both general sub-Gaussian TensorRIP claims are false as stated. The KaczTIHT theorem separately assumes isotropy, so this omission does not itself invalidate that restricted application.
issues.title: The common sub-Gaussian RIP hypotheses omit isotropy
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local normalization hypothesis; the intended normalized Gaussian and Rademacher ensembles and the stated sample-size rates survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Given a collection of measurement matrices $\{\mat{A}_i \in \R^{m \times n_i}\}_{i \in [d]}$ we define a measurement operator that acts on the space of tensors via the \emph{face-splitting product} of these matrices.

issues.failure_explanation: Independence across component matrices supplies no independence between different rows within a component. For example, let every row of A_i equal one random vector v_i, with the v_i independent across i. The component matrices are independent, but all rows of their face-splitting product are identical.

failure_location.quote: That is, if the component matrices $\mat{A}_i$ are independent random matrices, then the rows of $\mat{A}$ are independent and each row is a Kronecker product of the respective rows of the component matrices:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add independence across row indices within each component matrix to this assertion.
issues.overall_effect: The stated distributional property of a general face-splitting product is false. Later results that explicitly require independent rows or entries avoid this defect.
issues.title: Independence of component matrices does not imply independence of product rows
issues.why_classification: A local independence condition repairs the assertion without changing the ensembles used in the subsequent analysis.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement lacks φ>0, which its proof needs. For a concrete counterexample, use independent Rademacher factors and write N=n^d. With φ=−3 and m=N³<N⁴, the normalized empirical Gram matrix satisfies E||m⁻¹AᵀA−I||_F²≤N²/m→0. Thus RIP holds with probability tending to one, contrary to the asserted limit zero.

issues.title: The RIP impossibility statement permits noncompressive exponents
issues.why_classification: The correction excludes noncompressive parameter choices while preserving the advertised polynomial-compression obstruction.

issues.failure_explanation: Take n=1 and independent Rademacher u and v. Their product has absolute value one surely. For 0<t<ℓ⁻², the left side is one, whereas the stated right side is strictly less than one for every C>0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a prefactor such as 2, with adjusted absolute constants, or state the bound only above a fixed positive threshold.
issues.overall_effect: The all-threshold concentration statement is false, although its later large-threshold uses can retain the same asymptotic rates.
issues.title: The inner-product tail bound cannot hold for every positive threshold
issues.why_classification: This is a local tail-bound correction that leaves the substantive concentration rates and downstream asymptotic conclusions unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Here, $C_1, C_2$ and $c \in \R^{+}$ are constants that can depend on the sub-Gaussian norm of the entries of $\mat{A}_i$'s.
for $m$ of the same order up to the logarithms and an additional $d$-factor

issues.failure_explanation: The proof requires C^d, but both displayed sampling bounds and the informal comparison suppress this dependence. It is genuinely necessary: take entries equal to zero with probability 1/2 and to ±√2 with probability 1/4 each. A coordinate rank-one tensor then has a nonzero measurement with probability 2⁻ᵈ per row. For fixed n and r=1, the stated polynomial-in-d sample sizes produce only zero measurements with probability tending to one.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain an exponential C₀^d factor in both sample-size bounds and revise the informal comparison, or explicitly restrict to fixed d while allowing exponentially d-dependent constants.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised polynomial dependence on tensor order, and the comparison with unstructured measurements up to logarithms and a d-factor, are false.
issues.title: The uniform trimming theorem drops exponential dependence on tensor order
issues.why_classification: Every supported correction loses the advertised polynomial-in-order rate or excludes variable tensor order, a material loss in the dimensional guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consider a measurement matrix $\mat{A} \in \R^{m \times n}$, and any $\vx \in \R^n$ and $m > k > 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated sampling bounds and listed constant dependencies omit φ. For fixed n>1 and an m satisfying those bounds, an allowed sufficiently large φ gives k≥m, violating the trimming definition. The proof also explicitly needs the omitted φ log n contribution to the sample count.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the confidence contribution φ log n in the sample requirement and require k<m, or declare φ fixed and allow the constants to depend on it.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem does not define its embedding for all stated parameters and does not support its arbitrary confidence exponent.
issues.title: The trimming confidence parameter can make the construction undefined
issues.why_classification: This is a local confidence and admissibility correction; the intended fixed-confidence sample-size orders remain unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Now, note that (e.g., \cite[Lemma 2]{zhang2018median}), $\|\vu_{(k)} - \vv_{(k)}\| \leq \|\vu-\vv\|_\infty$ for any two vectors $\vu$ and $\vv$ and their $k$-th order statistics.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited order-statistic stability applies to ordered values, not signed values reordered by magnitude. For measurement vectors (a,−b) and (b,−a), with 0<a<b and b−a arbitrarily small, retaining the smallest magnitude produces a and −a. Their difference stays near 2a while the original vectors' infinity-norm difference tends to zero.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry out the comparison with sorted absolute measurement values. Their Euclidean norms equal the required trimmed norms, and the order-statistic estimate then applies.
issues.overall_effect: The net-to-continuum extension uses a false Lipschitz estimate.
issues.title: Absolute-value sorting does not stabilize the signed measurement vector
issues.why_classification: A short local modification of the auxiliary vectors repairs the argument without changing the embedding, sample rates, or claimed norm guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: A lower bound on m does not imply linear, or even polynomial, growth in n. Even with d and φ fixed, the theorem permits m=exp(n²), for which the displayed row-union bound is vacuous. Thus the asserted bound on P(E₁) does not follow over the theorem's full sampling range.

failure_location.quote: since the chosen $m$ scales linearly with $n$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use an m-uniform norm event instead: E||A||_F²=n^d and Markov give ||A||_F≤n^{(d+φ)/2} outside probability n⁻φ. Apply the resulting Lipschitz bound to the minimum over retained-row subset norms, choose the correspondingly finer net, and update its entropy/sample bound.
issues.overall_effect: The high-probability uniform extension is unproved for unrestricted m above the stated threshold.
issues.title: The row-norm probability argument assumes an unstated upper bound on m
issues.why_classification: A contained replacement of the probability argument and re-selection of the net mesh are needed, but the same trimming and covering architecture can be retained.

issues.overall_effect: The principal concentration input for trimmed measurements is false under its stated assumptions.

issues.failure_explanation: Union bounding p pointwise events at failure level α gives pα, not α. Using α/p also changes the estimator to k=log(8p/α); increasing m alone does not justify keeping the old k. The downstream uniform claim is actually false at its advertised budget: for Gaussian factors, form a rank-one tensor from normalized sums of 2k row factors in each mode. When k=Θ(log n), its 2k aligned raw squared measurements are of order (n/k)^d. At least k survive trimming, giving squared embedded norm at least of order n^d/(m k^{d−1}), which diverges at m=Θ(n log n) for fixed d≥2.

failure_location.quote: The desired result follows by the union bound argument.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use k=⌈log(8p/α)⌉ for finite sets. In the covering argument this becomes k of order log|N|+φ log n, and all theorem statements and algorithmic interpretations must reflect that larger trimming budget.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-set simultaneous guarantee and the claimed uniform low-rank guarantee after removing only logarithmically many rows fail.
issues.title: The union bound increases the required trimming budget, not just m

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \emph{Measurement matrix} $\mat{A} \in \R^{m\times n_1  n_2 \dots  n_d}$ \emph{with rows} $\va_{i} \in \R^{n_1  n_2 \dots  n_d}$ for $i \in [m]$

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm's input contract does not exclude zero rows. Such a row produces division by zero, including 0/0 in the noiseless case. Assumption 1 excludes this only for the later convergence theorem, not for the stated general procedure.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require nonzero rows or explicitly skip zero rows before performing normalized Kaczmarz updates.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm is not defined for every measurement matrix admitted by its input specification.
issues.title: KaczTIHT is undefined on allowed zero-row inputs
issues.why_classification: A standard local input condition or zero-row preprocessing step preserves the method and all stated convergence guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm retains m_trim rows and multiplies their gradient sum by m/m_trim. The matrix used in the theorem instead produces multiplier m/(m−m_trim). These are different updates except when m_trim=m/2. Moreover, retaining m_trim smallest measurements is not the claimed removal of m_trim largest measurements.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use m_trim consistently as the number removed: retain the first m−m_trim indices and require 0≤m_trim<m. Then the algorithm's multiplier and the defined trimmed matrix agree.
issues.overall_effect: The deterministic analysis and the connection to the trimmed embedding theorem do not apply to Algorithm TrimTIHT as written.
issues.title: The analyzed trimmed gradient differs from the algorithm's gradient
issues.why_classification: A local retained-versus-removed count correction aligns the procedure with its intended analysis without a new convergence argument or loss of the intended guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes ||R^{t+1}||≤c_t||R^t||. It yields a product of the historical factors, not c_t^{t+1}. For an identity gradient and exact thresholding, take successive step sizes 0.01 and 0.99. The residual after two updates is 0.0099 times the initial residual, whereas the claimed bound using the last factor is (2·0.01)²=0.0004.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the one-step estimate and iterate it as ∏_{s=0}^t c_s. A geometric bound q^{t+1} requires an explicit common bound c_s≤q for every preceding step.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's global path-dependent error bound is false, although the proved one-step estimate survives.
issues.title: A time-varying one-step factor is incorrectly raised to the iteration count
issues.why_classification: The repair weakens the quantitative conclusion to a history-dependent product, while retaining the existing proof and a comparable conditional convergence result.

issues.failure_explanation: No hypothesis prevents A_t r^t=0. In that case u_t=0 and ρ_t is 0/0, even when the residual is nonzero. At exact recovery, Δ_t is also 0/0. The theorem and supporting comparisons nevertheless purport to apply to all iterations of general measurements.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Treat zero residuals separately and define ρ_t=0 when A_t r^t=0. The latter case has zero gradient, and the relevant inequalities can be checked directly without division.
issues.overall_effect: The path bound and the ρ_t-versus-Δ_t claims are not defined in kernel and exact-recovery cases admitted by the hypotheses.
issues.title: The path-analysis quotients are undefined at legitimate residuals
issues.why_classification: These are local degenerate-case conventions and checks; no convergence rate or intended measurement regime must be lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited CP approximation guarantee contains an additive error independent of ε, whereas Assumption 2 is purely relative. If U^k=X*, Assumption 2 requires exact output, but the cited guarantee permits positive error. More generally, as the residual tends to zero, choosing ε alone cannot absorb a fixed additive floor. Thus the asserted automatic realization is not established.

failure_location.quote: The same is true for the low rank CP thresholding using Theorem~\ref{thm:opt_cp_approx} for a suitably chosen $\varepsilon$ under mild assumptions.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the invocation by an explicit additive-error budget. For ε=ξ, it suffices that the additive term be at most (ξ+ξ²)||U^k−X*||². Without such control, retain Assumption 2 as an additional hypothesis rather than claiming the cited routine ensures it.
issues.overall_effect: The proposed CP implementation of the fitting assumption is unsupported. The KaczTIHT theorem remains a conditional statement when Assumption 2 is imposed independently.
issues.title: The CP fitting theorem does not automatically supply pure relative accuracy
issues.why_classification: The correction removes an automatic computational guarantee near convergence, but leaves the conditional CP convergence theorem and the HOSVD realization intact.
